title: SSE loss-tolerant chunk indexing + authenticated resume handshake
creator: Anita Lopez
description: Implement an SSE resume handshake that allows clients to reconnect after transient network failures without replaying already-applied function/tool calls, while also authenticating chunk boundaries. The design should be loss-tolerant for single-chunk loss, minimize round-trips, and be compatible with existing JSONL framing clients.
background: We currently support basic SSE reconnect tokens but have seen production incidents where resumed sessions either re-executed idempotent-sensitive tool calls or produced duplicate structured output fragments. Customers running private and dedicated deployments require authenticated resume semantics for compliance and auditability. This ticket explores a hybrid approach: chunk indexing (per-stream monotonic offsets), a short-lived resume token delegation tied to TLS session fingerprint and client id, and an HMAC-signed chunk manifest to allow the server and client to reconcile missing fragments without re-running tool calls.
proposal: 1) Introduce a per-session chunk index (0-based) emitted as metadata with each SSE chunk: `X-Chunk-Index: <n>`. 2) Emit periodic lightweight snapshots (every 8 chunks or on function-call boundaries) containing a small resume manifest: {last_index, last_tool_call_id, manifest_hmac}. 3) On reconnect, client supplies `Resume-Token` and `Last-Received-Index` headers. Server validates token, checks manifest_hmac to ensure boundary integrity, and decides whether to (a) resume directly from next index, (b) send a replay of missing payloads (non-functional bodies only), or (c) require a fallback full re-run for tool-call safety. 4) Use HMAC with per-tenant key (via KMS/HSM) to sign manifests. 5) Add backpressure hint header `X-Client-Window` to coordinate server flushes when clients reconnect frequently.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits X-Chunk-Index and a resume manifest at configured intervals (default 8 chunks)
Resume-Token validation flow exists and rejects tokens older than token_ttl (default 5 minutes)
Resume path avoids re-executing tool calls when manifest_hmac validates and last_tool_call_id matches server state
Unit + integration tests simulate single-chunk loss, multi-chunk loss within window, and tool-call boundary disconnects
Security signoff confirming per-tenant HMAC key usage and KMS access audit
Console telemetry dashboard shows resumed sessions vs full restarts and duplicate tool-call incidents down by 90% in synthetic test
tasks: Spec: finalize manifest format and header names (team: infra + runtime)
Runtime: emit chunk-index header and embed manifest JSON in SSE comment frames
Auth: implement per-tenant resume-token issuance and short TTLs, integrate with KMS
Server: validate manifest_hmac on reconnect and decide resume policy
Client SDK: add reconnect helper that reads chunk-index and stores last successful manifest
E2E: write tests for idempotent tool-call boundaries and reassembly correctness
Docs: update API streaming section with examples and migration guidance
Observability: add metrics for resume-success-rate, token-invalid-rate, and duplicate-tool-call-count
design_decisions: Use HMAC over manifest rather than encrypting payloads to keep manifests small and verifiable without extra KMS calls per reconnect
Snapshot interval defaults to 8 chunks — trade-off: more frequent snapshots increases safety but adds metadata overhead
Resume-Token includes a server-issued nonce + tenant id + expiry and is rotated per-stream to limit replay risk
If manifest_hmac fails but last_tool_call_id unchanged, server will send a compact delta (without re-running calls) where possible; otherwise fall back to full replay policy
risks: Increased metadata could raise tokenization/ingestion costs for very high-throughput streams
Mis-synchronized last_tool_call_id between stateless frontends and backend store could cause false fallbacks — requires careful atomic persistence
Complexity in client SDKs across languages could delay adoption and lead to inconsistent behavior
KMS latency could affect resume validation; mitigate with short-lived derived keys cached by frontends
open_questions: Should manifest snapshots be anchored on function-call boundaries only (safer) or time/chunk intervals (more resumability)?
What is the exact resume token TTL policy for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments?
How to surface partial replay to customers in a way that lets them opt-in/out of strict resume semantics?
Can we piggyback manifest HMAC verification on existing auth middleware to avoid path duplication?
implementation_notes:
- Add `X-Chunk-Index` header in the runtime response writer.
- Emit manifest as an SSE comment like `:manifest {json}` to remain HTTP-eventstream-compatible.
- Resume endpoint accepts `Resume-Token` and `Last-Received-Index` headers; if both present, validate token, look up last manifest for that token, compare indices.
- Use KMS to sign per-tenant derived HMAC keys; store derived key cache per frontend for TTL duration.
- For private deployments, fall back to tenant-managed HMAC keys with optional VPC KMS integration.
- Add feature flag `sse.authenticated_resume` rollout to canary before enabling globally.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests: manifest generation, HMAC verification, token parsing.
- Integration: multi-client reconnect tests with a simulated flaky network, asserting no duplicate function call side effects.
- Chaos: introduce chunk drop and reorder to verify client reassembly logic.
- Performance: benchmark metadata overhead at 10k rps streaming with default 8-chunk snapshot interval.
observability:
New metrics: `stream.resume.attempts`, `stream.resume.success`, `stream.resume.fallbacks`, `stream.duplicate_tool_calls`, `stream.manifest.hmac_failures`.
Trace events: emit `resume.handshake.start` and `resume.handshake.result` with tags {tenant, model, route}.
Alert: page on `stream.duplicate_tool_calls` > 5% in 1h for production clusters.
migration_notes: Backward-compatible: clients without resume support continue to reconnect using existing token expiry flows. Documented header names and SDK helpers will be published in the runtime-2.4 release notes. For Dedicated/Private customers, enable via console toggle to allow staged onboarding.
